note: Fraction redesign development cases (2026-11-19), written from testsuite/fraction-blueprint.json. Each case's teacher_picture was written before its prompt and says what a good teacher draws for that exact question, independent of any card. Used for design and tuning. The scoring set is separate: written by a fresh agent from the blueprint alone, sealed, and never used for tuning (its SHA-256 is recorded in docs/FRACTION_REDESIGN_2026-11-19.md). Never taken from the question set. Mix: 12 questions, 7 detailed requests, 5 topic names; 5 in Chinese. All under the case-overlap bars (0.20 open, 0.15 held-out); FD-06 first came out identical to an open question and was rewritten.

cases.teacher_picture: A rectangle (the brownie) cut into 2 equal parts, one shaded and labelled 1/2; beside it the same rectangle cut into a big and a small piece, labelled 'not halves'.
cases.prompt: My son cut a brownie in two and says we each got half, but one piece is way bigger. Is that still a half?

cases.teacher_picture: A circle cut into 2 equal parts with one shaded (1/2), and a circle cut into 3 equal parts with one shaded (1/3).
cases.prompt: 认识二分之一和三分之一

cases.teacher_picture: A bar cut into 6 equal parts, each labelled 1/6; 5 parts shaded and counted 1/6, 2/6, ... 5/6.
cases.prompt: My kid reads 5/6 as 'five sixes'. What does the 5 in 5/6 actually count?

cases.teacher_picture: 4 identical bars, each cut into 3 equal parts, all shaded; labelled 12/3 = 4.
cases.prompt: My daughter's worksheet asks her to write 4 as a fraction with a denominator of 3 and she's completely stuck. How do I explain it to her?

cases.teacher_picture: Three identical bars stacked: halves with 1 shaded, fourths with 2 shaded, eighths with 4 shaded; the shaded lengths line up.
cases.prompt: Equivalent fractions

cases.teacher_picture: Two identical bars: one in sixths with 3 shaded, one in tenths with 5 shaded; the shaded lengths line up at the half mark; labelled 3/6 = 5/10 = 1/2.
cases.prompt: 我家老二坚持说六分之三比十分之五大，因为六比十小，切的块更大。怎么跟她解释这两个其实一样多？

cases.teacher_picture: Two identical circles: 5/8 and 2/3 shaded; both re-cut into 24ths (15/24 and 16/24); written 5/8 < 2/3.
cases.prompt: My brother and I are arguing: which is the bigger slice of the same pie, 5/8 or 2/3?

cases.teacher_picture: Two identical bars: 3/4 and 3/8 shaded; fewer, bigger pieces in fourths; written 3/4 > 3/8.
cases.prompt: Same top number, different bottom number: which fraction wins

cases.teacher_picture: One circle cut into 8 equal parts: 2 shaded in one colour, the next 3 in another; written 2/8 + 3/8 = 5/8.
cases.prompt: I ate 2/8 of a cake and my sister ate 3/8. How much of the cake did we eat together?

cases.teacher_picture: One bar cut into 10 equal parts: 7 shaded, 3 of them crossed out, 4 left; written 7/10 − 3/10 = 4/10. The parts stay tenths, so the denominator stays 10.
cases.prompt: 孩子做 7/10 − 3/10，写成了 4/0，说分子减分子、分母减分母。我该怎么跟他讲为什么不对？

cases.teacher_picture: 3 identical bars cut into thirds: 2 fully shaded and 1 third of the third bar shaded; the thirds counted to 7; written 2 1/3 = 7/3.
cases.prompt: How do I turn 2 1/3 into an improper fraction?

cases.teacher_picture: 5 bars, each with 3 of 4 parts shaded (5 copies of 3/4); the 15 fourths regrouped into 3 whole bars and 3/4; written 5 x 3/4 = 15/4 = 3 3/4 cups.
cases.prompt: We're baking five batches of muffins for the school fair and each batch takes 3/4 cup of flour. My son asked how much flour we have to buy altogether. Can you show him?

cases.teacher_picture: A hundred grid with 5 full columns shaded: 5 tenths = 50 hundredths; written 0.5 = 5/10 = 50/100 = 0.50.
cases.prompt: Grandpa here. Junior insists 0.50 is bigger than 0.5 because it has more digits. How do I convince him?

cases.teacher_picture: One fully shaded hundred grid (1) and a second grid with 2 columns and 5 squares shaded (0.25); written 1.25 = 1 + 25/100.
cases.prompt: In science my daughter recorded that her bean plant grew 1.25 cm this week. She asked what the .25 part actually means. How do I explain it?

cases.teacher_picture: A bar for 2/5 and a bar for 1/4, both re-cut into twentieths (8/20 and 5/20), then joined on one bar: 13/20; written 2/5 + 1/4 = 8/20 + 5/20 = 13/20, not 3/9.
cases.prompt: I wrote 2/5 + 1/4 = 3/9 and the teacher marked it wrong. Why?

cases.teacher_picture: 2 bars (sandwiches), each cut into 5 equal parts; each person takes one fifth from each sandwich; one person's 2 fifths marked; written 2 / 5 = 2/5 of a sandwich each.
cases.prompt: Five of us are splitting 2 sandwiches evenly at lunch. How much sandwich does each person get?

cases.teacher_picture: A tape labelled 3 m cut into 4 equal pieces, each labelled 3/4 m; written 3 ÷ 4 = 3/4.
cases.prompt: 分数与除法的关系

cases.teacher_picture: A tape for 24 children cut into 8 equal parts, each labelled 3; 3 parts marked; 9 children; written 3/8 of 24 = 9.
cases.prompt: There are 24 kids in my class and the teacher said 3/8 of us walk to school. I need to work out how many kids walk, and I don't know where to start.

cases.teacher_picture: A unit square (the acre) cut into 5 columns with 3 shaded one way, and 2 rows with 1 shaded the other way; the overlap is 3 of 10 small rectangles; written 1/2 x 3/5 = 3/10 acre.
cases.prompt: A garden plot is 3/5 of an acre and half of it is planted with tomatoes. What part of an acre is tomatoes, and why does the answer come out smaller?

cases.teacher_picture: 3 bars (cups), each cut into 4 quarters; the quarter scoops counted 1 to 12; written 3 / (1/4) = 12.
cases.prompt: My daughter's homework asks how many 1/4-cup scoops are in 3 cups of rice. She got 12 but thinks it must be wrong because dividing should make it smaller. How do I explain?

cases.teacher_picture: A bar (the lasagna) cut into thirds with one third left; that third cut into 2 equal pieces; the other thirds shown cut the same way to count sixths; one piece is 1/6 of the lasagna; written 1/3 / 2 = 1/6.
cases.prompt: There's 1/3 of a lasagna left and two of us want to split it evenly. What fraction of the whole lasagna does each of us get?

cases.teacher_picture: A hundred grid with 35 squares shaded; written 35% = 35/100.
cases.prompt: Percentages explained

cases.teacher_picture: Two tapes of equal unit blocks: red 3 blocks, yellow 2 blocks; 5 blocks = 15 cups, so each block is 3 cups: red 9, yellow 6. A fraction-of-one-whole card would mislead.
cases.prompt: Our paint mix is 3 cups of red for every 2 cups of yellow. We need 15 cups of paint for the mural. My son is trying to work out how many cups of each to use.

cases.teacher_picture: A before tape (80 yuan) and an after tape (100 yuan), the 20-yuan increase marked against 80: 20/80 = 25%. A single fraction card would mislead.
cases.prompt: 一件衣服原价 80 元，现在卖 100 元，涨了百分之几？
